title.zh: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋
title.en: Volume 391 Biographies 178: Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong
title.raw: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋

sentences.zh: 倭仁，字艮峰，烏齊格里氏，蒙古正紅旗人，河南駐防。

translations.literal: Wo Ren, style name Genfeng, of the Ujikri clan, a Mongol of the Plain Red Banner, garrisoned at Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren, whose style was Genfeng, belonged to the Ujikri clan. A Mongol bannerman of the Plain Red Banner, he was stationed on garrison duty in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1829 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷中允、侍講、侍讀、庶子、侍講學士、侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as middle attendant, lecturer, reader, tutor of the heir apparent, lecturer-at-large, and reader-at-large.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of middle attendant, lecturer, reader, tutor of the heir apparent, and finally lecturer-at-large and reader-at-large.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to be president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 he was transferred to the presidency of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「行政莫先於用人，用人莫先於君子小人之辨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, in response to an edict he submitted a memorial, stating in part: 'In administration nothing comes before employing men; in employing men nothing comes before distinguishing gentlemen from petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor acceded, Wo Ren answered an imperial call for counsel with a memorial that began: 'In governing, nothing precedes the choice of men; in choosing men, nothing precedes telling the gentleman from the petty man.

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人藏於心術者難知，發於事蹟者易見。

translations.literal: As for gentlemen and petty men, what is hidden in the mind is hard to know; what appears in deeds is easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: What a gentleman or a petty man keeps in the heart is hard to discern; what shows in his conduct is easy to see.

sentences.zh: 大抵君子訥拙，小人佞巧；

translations.literal: Generally, gentlemen are slow-spoken and awkward; petty men are flattering and clever;
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, the gentleman is plain-spoken and unadorned, the petty man glib and artful;

sentences.zh: 君子澹定，小人躁競；

translations.literal: gentlemen are calm and settled; petty men are restless and contentious;
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman is calm and self-possessed, the petty man restless and grasping;

sentences.zh: 君子愛惜人才，小人排擠異類；

translations.literal: gentlemen cherish talent; petty men drive out those unlike themselves;
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman cherishes able men, the petty man drives out anyone unlike himself;

sentences.zh: 君子圖遠大，以國家元氣為先，小人計目前，以聚斂刻薄為務。

translations.literal: Gentlemen plan for the long term and put the nation's vital energy first; petty men reckon only the present and make extortion and meanness their task.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman looks to the long view and puts the nation's underlying strength first; the petty man counts only the moment and makes squeezing revenue and harshness his business.

sentences.zh: 剛正不撓、無所阿鄉者，君子也；

translations.literal: Those who are upright and unyielding and curry favor with no one are gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: He who is upright, unbending, and curries favor with none is a gentleman;

sentences.zh: 依違兩可、工於趨避者，小人也。

translations.literal: those who waver between two sides and are skilled at evasion are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: he who trims between two sides and is skilled at slipping away is a petty man.

sentences.zh: 諫諍匡弼、進憂危之議，動人主之警心者，君子也；

translations.literal: Those who remonstrate and assist, who advance warnings of peril to stir the ruler's vigilance, are gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: He who admonishes and steadies the throne, who offers words of peril to rouse the sovereign's vigilance, is a gentleman;

sentences.zh: 喜言氣數、不畏天變，長人君之逸志者，小人也。

translations.literal: those who delight in speaking of fate and portents and do not fear Heaven's changes, who foster the sovereign's mind of ease, are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: he who delights in omens and fate, who does not fear Heaven's warnings and instead feeds the ruler's wish for ease, is a petty man.

sentences.zh: 公私邪正，相反如此。

translations.literal: Public and private, straight and crooked—so opposed are they.
translations.idiomatic: Between public duty and private interest, between the straight and the crooked, the contrast is as stark as this.

sentences.zh: 皇上天亶聰明，孰賢孰否，必能洞知。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-bestowed intelligence—who is worthy and who is not, you must surely discern to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Heaven-given discernment can surely see through who is worthy and who is not.

sentences.zh: 第恐一人之心思耳目，揣摩者眾，混淆者多，幾微莫辨，情偽滋紛，愛憎稍涉偏私，取捨必至失當。

translations.literal: Only I fear that with one man's thoughts and senses, those who study his wishes are many and those who confuse him many; the subtle becomes impossible to distinguish, sincerity and falsehood multiply, and if love and hate involve the slightest bias, choice and rejection must go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that a single mind and pair of ears, however keen, must face many who read your wishes and many who cloud them; the finest shades grow hard to tell apart, truth and pretense tangle, and the slightest tilt of favor or dislike will skew whom you keep and whom you cast aside.

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，豈有他術，在皇上好學勤求，使聖志益明，聖德日固而已。

translations.literal: To know men is to be wise—what other art is there? It lies only in Your Majesty's diligent study and seeking, so that the sage purpose grows clearer and sage virtue daily firmer.
translations.idiomatic: To know men is wisdom: there is no other secret. Your Majesty must study earnestly and seek counsel without cease, so your sage purpose grows ever clearer and your sage virtue firmer day by day.

sentences.zh: 宋程顥雲，'古者人君必有誦訓箴諫之臣'。

translations.literal: Song Cheng Hao said, 'In antiquity the ruler must have ministers who recite admonitions and offer remonstrance.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao of the Song said, 'In ancient times every ruler had ministers who recited lessons and offered frank remonstrance.'

sentences.zh: 請命老成之儒，講論道義，又擇天下賢俊，陪侍法從。

translations.literal: I beg that aged Confucians be ordered to discourse on moral principle, and that worthy men from throughout the realm be chosen to attend in the ruler's entourage.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that seasoned Confucians be charged to expound the Way and its duties, and that worthy men from across the realm be chosen to attend you in study and counsel.

sentences.zh: 我朝康熙間，熊賜履上疏，亦以'延訪真儒'為說。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's Kangxi reign, Xiong Cili memorialized likewise urging 'extending visits to true Confucians.'
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign of our dynasty, Xiong Cili likewise memorialized the throne, urging that true scholars be sought out and consulted.

sentences.zh: 二臣所言，皆修養身心之要，用人行政之源也。

translations.literal: What these two ministers said is all essential to cultivating body and mind, the source of employing men and governing.
translations.idiomatic: What these two ministers urged goes to the heart of self-cultivation—and to the root of how men are chosen and how the realm is governed.

sentences.zh: 天下治亂系宰相，君德成就責講筵。

translations.literal: Order and disorder in the realm hinge on the chief minister; achievement of the ruler's virtue rests with the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the realm is well or ill governed hangs on the chief minister; whether the ruler's virtue matures rests on those who teach him.

sentences.zh: 惟君德成就而後輔弼得人，輔弼得人而後天下可治。」

translations.literal: Only when the ruler's virtue is achieved may the assistants be well chosen; only when assistants are well chosen may the realm be governed.'
translations.idiomatic: Only when the ruler's virtue is formed can the right helpers be found; only when the right helpers are found can the realm be brought to order.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，上稱其切直，因諭大小臣工進言以倭仁為法。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor praised its forthrightness and instructed officials great and small to speak frankly with Wo Ren as their model.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor praised its blunt honesty and told officials at every rank to speak their minds, taking Wo Ren as their example.

sentences.zh: 未幾，禮部侍郎曾國籓奏用人三策，上复憶倭仁言，手詔同褒勉焉。

translations.literal: Before long, Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan memorialized with three policies for employing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's words and personally issued an edict praising them together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan submitted three proposals on appointing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's memorial and with his own hand issued an edict commending them both.

sentences.zh: 尋予副都統銜，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the rank of vice banner commander and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted the rank of vice banner commander and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 大理寺少卿田雨公疏言倭仁用違其才，上曰：「邊疆要任，非投閒置散也。

translations.literal: Assistant President of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Yugong memorialized that Wo Ren's assignment did not suit his talents; the Emperor said, 'Frontier duties are important posts, not idle banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant President Tian Yugong of the Court of Judicial Review argued that Wo Ren's talents were wasted on the assignment; the Emperor replied, 'A frontier post is a weighty charge, not a place to shelve a man in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 若以外任皆左遷，豈國家文武兼資、內外並重之意乎？」

translations.literal: If every post outside the capital were treated as demotion, would that accord with the state's purpose of valuing both civil and military talent and weighing inner and outer posts equally?'
translations.idiomatic: If every appointment beyond the capital were read as a demotion, how would that square with the state's aim to draw on both civil and military talent and to weigh service at court and in the provinces alike?'

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，倭仁复上敬陳治本一疏，上謂其意在責難陳善，尚無不合，惟僅泛語治道，因戒以留心邊務，勿託空言。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Wo Ren again submitted a memorial on founding governance at the root; the Emperor said his intent was to admonish and offer good counsel and was not improper, but that he spoke only in generalities of governing the Way, and cautioned him to attend to frontier affairs and not trust empty words.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 Wo Ren again submitted a memorial on getting governance right at the root. The Emperor said his aim—to admonish and offer honest counsel—was not out of line, but that he spoke only in broad platitudes about the Way of rule, and warned him to mind frontier business and not hide behind empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 候補道何桂珍上封事，言倭仁秉性忠貞，見理明決，生平言行不負所學，請任以艱鉅，未許。

translations.literal: Expectant circuit intendant He Guizhen submitted a sealed memorial saying Wo Ren's character was loyal and steadfast, his grasp of principle clear and decisive, his lifelong words and acts worthy of his learning, and asking that weighty duties be entrusted to him—not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant circuit intendant He Guizhen sent in a sealed memorial praising Wo Ren's loyalty, clarity of judgment, and conduct worthy of his learning, and asking that grave responsibilities be placed on him. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年，倭仁劾葉爾羌回部郡王阿奇木伯克愛瑪特攤派路費及護衛索贓等罪，詔斥未經確訊，率行參奏，下部議，降三級調用。

translations.literal: In the third year Wo Ren impeached Akhmet, district king and tribal chief of the Muslim communities at Yarkand, for levying travel expenses and extortion by his guards, among other crimes; an edict rebuked him for accusing without thorough investigation and ordered the ministry to deliberate; he was demoted three ranks and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 Wo Ren impeached Akhmet, the Yarkand district king and Akhun-beck, for forcing travelers to pay road levies and for his guards' demands for bribes. The throne rebuked him for acting without a full inquiry and sent the case to the ministries; Wo Ren was demoted three ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 四年，侍郎王茂廕等請命會同籌辦京師團練，上以軍務非所長，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Vice Minister Wang Maoyin and others asked that he be ordered to jointly organize capital militia training; the Emperor, saying military affairs were not his strength, shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 Vice Minister Wang Maoyin and others asked that Wo Ren be ordered to help organize militia training in the capital; the Emperor, saying military affairs were not his forte, set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 尋命以侍講候補入直上書房，授惇郡王讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to enter the Upper Study Hall as lecturer on the waiting list and teach the Prince of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered into the Upper Study as a lecturer on the waiting list to instruct the Prince of Dun.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to lecturer-at-large.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he was promoted to lecturer-at-large.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺卿、盛京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice president of the Mukden Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and as vice president of the Mukden Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 七年，調戶部，管奉天府尹事，劾罷盛京副都統增慶、兵部侍郎富呢雅杭阿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to the Board of Revenue and supervised affairs of the Fengtian governor-general; he impeached and dismissed Mukden vice president Zeng Qing and Board of War vice president Funiyahuang'a.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he was moved to the Board of Revenue and put in charge of the Fengtian governor-general's affairs; he impeached and removed Mukden vice president Zeng Qing and Board of War vice president Funiyahuang'a.

sentences.zh: 及頒詔中外，命充朝鮮正使。

translations.literal: When an edict was promulgated throughout the realm, he was appointed chief envoy to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: When a major edict was issued to the empire, he was appointed chief envoy to Korea.

sentences.zh: 召回京，授都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was made left censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was appointed left censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 兩宮皇太后以倭仁老成端謹，學問優長，命授穆宗讀。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers, because Wo Ren was seasoned, upright, and careful and his learning outstanding, ordered him to instruct the Tongzhi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers, finding Wo Ren seasoned, upright, and learned, ordered him to tutor the Tongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 倭仁輯古帝王事蹟，及古今名臣奏議，附說進之，賜名啟心金鑑，置弘德殿資講肄。

translations.literal: Wo Ren compiled deeds of ancient emperors and memorials of famous ministers through the ages, with commentary, and presented them; they were given the title Heart-Opening Golden Mirror and placed in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for lecture and study.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren compiled the deeds of ancient rulers and memorials of renowned ministers past and present, added his own commentary, and presented the work to the throne. It was named the Heart-Opening Golden Mirror and kept in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for the emperor's study.

sentences.zh: 倭仁素嚴正，穆宗尤敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Wo Ren had always been sternly upright; the Tongzhi Emperor especially respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren had always been stern and upright, and the Tongzhi Emperor held him in particular awe.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，調工部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, transferred to Minister of Works and appointed co-grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made concurrent chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, moved to Minister of Works, and appointed co-grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「河南自咸豐三年以後，粵、捻焚掠，蓋藏已空，州縣誅求仍復無厭。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating in part: 'Since the third year of Xianfeng in Henan, the Taiping and Nian rebels have burned and plundered until storehouses are empty, yet districts and counties still extort without surfeit.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: 'Since 1853 in Henan, Taiping and Nian bands have burned and looted until nothing is left in the granaries, yet the districts and counties still squeeze the people without end.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能盡擇州縣，則必慎擇督撫。

translations.literal: If the court cannot choose every district and county, it must carefully choose governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: If the court cannot pick every magistrate, it must at least choose governors-general and governors with care.

sentences.zh: 督撫不取之屬員，則屬員自無可挾以為恣睢之地。

translations.literal: If governors-general and governors do not take bribes from subordinates, subordinates naturally have nothing to rely on for arbitrary license.
translations.idiomatic: When governors do not profit from their staffs, those staffs have no footing on which to tyrannize the people.

sentences.zh: 今日河南積習，祗曰民刁詐，不曰官貪庸；

translations.literal: Today's entrenched habit in Henan is only to call the people crafty and deceitful, not to call officials greedy and incompetent;
translations.idiomatic: The standing habit in Henan today is to blame only the people's craftiness, never the officials' greed and incompetence;

sentences.zh: 祗狃於愚民之抗官，不思所以致抗之由。

translations.literal: only to cling to the notion that foolish commoners resist officials, without thinking what causes that resistance.
translations.idiomatic: only to fix on the idea that ignorant peasants defy their magistrates, without asking what drives them to defiance.

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷慎察大吏，力挽積習，寇亂之源，庶幾可弭。」

translations.literal: It lies only in the court's carefully scrutinizing great officials and forcefully reversing entrenched habits—then the source of banditry may perhaps be stilled.'
translations.idiomatic: Only if the court scrutinizes its senior appointees and forcefully breaks these habits can the roots of rebellion perhaps be cut.'

sentences.zh: 是年秋，拜文淵閣大學士，疏劾新授廣東巡撫黃贊湯貪詐，解其職。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth and memorialized to impeach the newly appointed Guangdong governor Huang Zantang for greed and fraud, securing his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and memorialized against the newly appointed Guangdong governor Huang Zantang for greed and deceit, bringing about his removal.

sentences.zh: 六年，同文館議考選正途五品以下京外官入館肄習天文算學，聘西人為教習。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Tongwenguan proposed selecting regular-track officials of fifth rank and below from the capital and provinces to study astronomy and mathematics in the hall, hiring Westerners as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 the Tongwenguan proposed recruiting regular-track officials of fifth rank and below from court and provinces to study astronomy and mathematics there, with Westerners engaged as teachers.

sentences.zh: 倭仁謂根本之圖，在人心不在技藝，尤以西人教習為不可；

translations.literal: Wo Ren said the fundamental plan lies in men's hearts, not in techniques, and especially that Western instructors were unacceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren argued that the root lay in men's hearts, not in technical skill, and above all that Western teachers were intolerable;

sentences.zh: 且謂必習天文算學，應求中國能精其法者，上疏請罷議。

translations.literal: and said that if astronomy and mathematics must be studied, Chinese who mastered the methods should be sought; he memorialized asking that the proposal be dropped.
translations.idiomatic: and that if such studies were needed, Chinese masters of the methods should be found. He memorialized the throne to abandon the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是詔倭仁保薦，別設一館，即由倭仁督率講求。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Wo Ren to recommend men, set up a separate hall, and have Wo Ren supervise the study.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then ordered Wo Ren to nominate teachers, open a separate hall, and direct the instruction himself.

sentences.zh: 復奏意中並無其人，不敢妄保。

translations.literal: He memorialized again that he had no one in mind and dared not recommend rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He replied again that he knew no one fit for the task and dared not nominate anyone lightly.

sentences.zh: 尋命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 倭仁屢疏懇辭，不允；

translations.literal: Wo Ren repeatedly memorialized earnestly to decline; it was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren repeatedly begged off in memorials, without success;

sentences.zh: 因稱疾篤，乞休，命解兼職，仍在弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: he then claimed grave illness and begged retirement; he was ordered relieved of concurrent posts but to remain at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he then pleaded grave illness and asked to retire; the court released him from his extra duties but kept him at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言大婚典禮宜崇節儉，及武英殿災，复偕徐桐、翁同龢疏請勤修聖德，停罷一切工程，以弭災變，並嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized that the grand wedding rites should honor frugality; when the Hall of Martial Glory burned, he again joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in memorializing to cultivate sage virtue diligently, halt all construction, and quell calamities—and all was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he urged frugality for the imperial wedding rites; after fire struck the Hall of Martial Glory, he joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in asking the emperor to deepen his virtue and halt all building projects to appease Heaven's warning—and the court welcomed their counsel.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉文華殿大學士，以疾再乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and again begged retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he was promoted to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall and again asked leave on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor, entered the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and honored with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. The court granted him the posthumous rank of Grand Tutor, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave him the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，河南巡撫李鶴年奏建專祠於開封，允之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu the Henan governor Li Henian memorialized to build a private shrine at Kaifeng; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 Henan governor Li Henian asked to erect a private shrine to Wo Ren at Kaifeng, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，曾國籓官京師，與倭仁、李棠階、吳廷棟、何桂珍、竇垿講求宋儒之學。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zeng Guofan held office in the capital, he joined Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan in studying Song Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years, while Zeng Guofan served in the capital, he studied Song Neo-Confucian thought together with Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan.

sentences.zh: 其後國籓出平大難，為中興名臣冠；

translations.literal: Afterward Guofan went out to quell great calamities and stood foremost among the Restoration statesmen;
translations.idiomatic: Later Guofan went forth to quell the great rebellions and became the leading statesman of the restoration;

sentences.zh: 倭仁作帝師，正色不阿；

translations.literal: Wo Ren served as imperial tutor, stern in countenance and yielding to none;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren served as the emperor's teacher, unbending in manner;

sentences.zh: 棠階、廷棟亦卓然有以自見焉。

translations.literal: Tangjie and Tingdong also distinguished themselves in their own right.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie and Tingdong likewise made names for themselves in their own spheres.

sentences.zh: 倭仁著有遺書十三卷。

translations.literal: Wo Ren left collected writings in thirteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren left posthumous writings in thirteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子福咸，江蘇鹽法道，署安徽徽寧池太廣道，咸豐十年，殉難寧國，贈太僕寺卿，騎都尉世職；

translations.literal: His son Fuxian was salt controller of Jiangsu and acting intendant of Huining, Chizhou, Taiping, and Guangde in Anhui; in the tenth year of Xianfeng he died at his post in Ningguo and was posthumously made vice president of the Court of Imperial Studs with a hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuxian served as Jiangsu salt controller and acting intendant over several Anhui circuits; in 1860 he died defending Ningguo and was posthumously made vice president of the Court of Imperial Studs, with a hereditary commandant's rank;

sentences.zh: 福裕，奉天府府尹。

translations.literal: Fuyu was governor of Fengtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu became governor of the Fengtian metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從子福潤，安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: His nephew Furun was governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Furun rose to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，外國兵入京師，闔家死焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu foreign troops entered the capital and the whole family perished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when foreign troops entered Beijing, the entire family died.

sentences.zh: 李棠階，字文園，河南河內人。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie, style name Wenyuan, was a native of Henei in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie, styled Wenyuan, came from Henei in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 五遷至侍讀。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of reader.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became a reader in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，督廣東學政，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted to vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he served as Guangdong education commissioner and was promoted to vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫黃恩彤奏請予鄉試年老武生職銜，嚴旨責譴，棠階亦因違例送考，議降三級調用，遂引疾家居。

translations.literal: When Governor Huang Entong memorialized to grant honorary titles to elderly military licentiates at the provincial examination, a stern edict rebuked him; Tangjie also, for violating regulations in presenting candidates, was ordered demoted three ranks and reassigned, and he pleaded illness and retired home.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Huang Entong asked to grant honorary ranks to aged military candidates at the provincial exams, the throne rebuked him sharply. Tangjie too, for irregularities in presenting candidates, was slated for demotion three ranks and transfer; he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，复日講，曾國籓薦棠階醇正堪備講官，召來京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, daily lectures resumed; Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as pure and upright and fit to serve as lecturer, and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor acceded, daily lectures resumed. Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as upright and fit to lecture the emperor, and he was called to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既而日講中輟，棠階以病未赴。

translations.literal: Before long daily lectures ceased; Tangjie, being ill, did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the daily lectures stopped again, and Tangjie, citing illness, never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，河北土寇蜂起，用尚書周祖培薦，命治河北團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Taiping rebels invaded north and local bandits rose throughout Hebei; on Minister Zhou Zupei's recommendation he was ordered to organize militia training in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, as Taiping forces pushed north and local bandits swarmed over Hebei, he was ordered—on Minister Zhou Zupei's recommendation—to organize militia defense in the province.

sentences.zh: 棠階聯絡村鎮，名曰「友助社」。

translations.literal: Tangjie linked villages and market towns under the name "Mutual Aid Society."
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie linked villages and market towns into units he called "Mutual Aid Society."

sentences.zh: 賊踞溫縣東河灘柳林，四出焚掠，棠階督團練擊之，村民未習戰，且無火器，殺賊數十人，卒不敵。

translations.literal: Bandits held the willow groves on the east river beach of Wen County and raided in all directions; Tangjie led the militia against them, but the villagers were untrained in warfare and had no firearms; they killed several dozen bandits but could not prevail in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits held the willow groves on Wen County's east river flats and raided far and wide. Tangjie led the militia against them, but the peasants were untrained and had no guns; though they killed several dozen bandits, they could not hold the field.

sentences.zh: 會山東巡撫李僡率兵至，賊引去。

translations.literal: When Shandong Governor Li Huang arrived with troops, the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong governor Li Huang arrived with troops, the bandits drew off.

sentences.zh: 賊自渡黃河，始知民間有備，稍稍牽綴。

translations.literal: From the time the bandits crossed the Yellow River they learned that the populace was prepared and were somewhat held back.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bandits crossed the Yellow River, they found the countryside armed and were somewhat slowed in their advance.

sentences.zh: 洎河北肅清，敘勞，加四品卿銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Hebei was pacified, his merit was recorded; he was given the rank of fourth-grade chamberlain and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was cleared, his service was rewarded with a fourth-grade chamberlain's rank and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，詔起用舊臣，棠階應召至。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict recalled former officials; Tangjie answered the summons and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 an edict recalled veteran officials; Tangjie answered the call and came to court.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「用人行政，惟在治心。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating: 'In employing men and governing, all lies in governing the heart.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: 'In appointing men and governing the realm, everything depends on governing the heart.

sentences.zh: 治心之要，莫先克己。

translations.literal: The essential of governing the heart is none other than self-restraint first.
translations.idiomatic: The first step in governing the heart is to restrain oneself.

sentences.zh: 請於師保匡弼之馀，豫杜左右近習之漸。

translations.literal: I beg that beyond the tutors who assist and correct, the gradual encroachment of those close at hand be forestalled in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the tutors who guide and correct you, I ask that you guard early against the slow encroachment of favorites at your side.

sentences.zh: 暇時進講通鑑、大學衍義諸書，以收物格意誠之效。」

translations.literal: In leisure hours advance lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and such books, to achieve the effect of investigating things and making the will sincere.'
translations.idiomatic: In your spare hours have read to you the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and works like them, so that you may reach the stage where things are understood and the will made sincere.'

sentences.zh: 又言：「紀綱之飭，在於嚴明賞罰。

translations.literal: He also said: 'To tighten discipline lies in making rewards and punishments strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'To restore discipline, rewards and punishments must be strict and clear.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷通諭諸事，務飭疆臣實力奉行，庶中外情志可通，而禍亂可弭。」

translations.literal: In all matters the court announces to the realm, frontier officials must be ordered to carry them out in earnest, so that sentiment within and without may connect and calamity and rebellion perhaps be stilled.'
translations.idiomatic: Every order the court sends to the provinces must be enforced in earnest by the frontier governors, so that court and country may speak with one mind and rebellion be checked.'

sentences.zh: 兩宮嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers welcomed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 授大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 先是兩江總督何桂清僨事逮治，部讞從重擬斬決，廷臣有右之者，言部臣有意畸重，仍從本律監候。

translations.literal: Earlier the Liangjiang governor-general He Guiqing, for bungling his charge, was arrested and tried; the ministry's finding proposed execution by decapitation with aggravation; some court officials supported him, saying the ministry intentionally weighed the penalty too heavily, and the sentence reverted to imprisonment awaiting execution under the original statute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liangjiang governor-general He Guiqing had been arrested for his failures in office. The ministries recommended aggravated decapitation, but some at court argued the penalty was skewed; the sentence was reduced to imprisonment awaiting execution under the standard law.

sentences.zh: 棠階疏謂桂清貽誤封疆罪大，不當輕比，非公論。

translations.literal: Tangjie memorialized that Guiqing's crime of harming the frontier was grave and should not be lightly compared—this was not public justice.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie memorialized that Guiqing's crime of ruining the frontier was too grave to be softened—that such leniency was not justice.

sentences.zh: 後桂清卒伏法。

translations.literal: Later Guiqing was executed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Guiqing was executed.

sentences.zh: 連擢禮部侍郎、左都御史，署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice minister of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in quick succession to vice minister of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and acting minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 召對，言：「治天下惟在安民，安民必先察吏。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he said: 'To govern the realm lies only in securing the people; to secure the people one must first scrutinize officials.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he said: 'To govern the realm is to settle the people; to settle the people you must first scrutinize your officials.

sentences.zh: 今日之盜賊，即昔日之良民，皆地方有司貪虐激之成變。

translations.literal: Today's bandits are yesterday's good commoners—all provoked into rebellion by the greed and cruelty of local officials.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits of today were the law-abiding people of yesterday, driven to revolt by the greed and cruelty of local magistrates.

sentences.zh: 為今日平亂計，非輕徭薄賦不能治本。

translations.literal: To pacify disorder today, without light levies and low taxes one cannot treat the root.
translations.idiomatic: To quell rebellion now, nothing will reach the root cause without lighter taxes and lighter corvée.

sentences.zh: 然非擇大吏，則守令不得其人，亦終不能收令行禁止之效。」

translations.literal: Yet unless great officials are chosen, prefects and magistrates will not be the right men, and in the end one cannot achieve the effect of orders issued and prohibitions enforced.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless senior appointees are chosen well, the prefects and magistrates below will be wrong men, and orders will never truly be obeyed.'

sentences.zh: 因極言河南亂事，及諸行省利病甚悉。

translations.literal: He then spoke at length on the disorders in Henan and on the benefits and harms of the various provinces in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to speak at length on the turmoil in Henan and on the strengths and failings of the provinces in painstaking detail.

sentences.zh: 命為軍機大臣，具疏力辭，弗許。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand councilor; he memorialized in detail earnestly to decline, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Grand Council, memorialized earnestly to decline, and was refused.

sentences.zh: 二年，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧克復，論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangning was recovered; for merit he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when Jiangning was recovered, he was rewarded with the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 大憝既平，上諭中外臣工以兢業交勉。

translations.literal: Once the great enemy was pacified, the Emperor instructed officials within and without to encourage one another in diligence.
translations.idiomatic: After the great rebellion was crushed, the emperor urged officials throughout the realm to exhort one another to diligence.

sentences.zh: 棠階語恭親王及同直諸大臣，謂當設誠致行，久而不懈，勿徒以空言相文飾，王深然之。

translations.literal: Tangjie spoke to Prince Gong and the other ministers on duty, saying they should set up sincerity and carry it into action, long without slackening, and not merely ornament one another with empty words; the prince deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie told Prince Gong and the other councilors on duty that they must act in earnest and keep at it, not dress one another in empty phrases. The prince strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 翼日召對，王反复陳君臣交儆之義，棠階與同僚繼言之，兩宮改容嘉納。

translations.literal: The next day at audience the prince repeatedly set forth the meaning of ruler and minister mutually admonishing one another; Tangjie and his colleagues followed with the same, and the two empress dowagers changed expression and praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the next day the prince spoke again and again on how ruler and ministers must warn each other; Tangjie and his colleagues added their voices, and the two empress dowagers listened with changed faces and welcomed the counsel.

sentences.zh: 尋調禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 太后命南書房、上書房諸臣纂輯前史事蹟，賜名治平寶鑑，命諸大臣進講。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered scholars of the Southern and Upper Study Halls to compile deeds from earlier histories; it was given the title Mirror of Ordered Peace and the great ministers were ordered to lecture on it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered scholars of the Southern and Upper Study to compile historical precedents; the work was named the Mirror of Ordered Peace, and senior ministers were told to lecture on it.

sentences.zh: 棠階因講漢文帝卻千里馬事，反复推言人主不宜有所嗜好，以啟窺伺之端。

translations.literal: Tangjie, lecturing on Emperor Wen of Han's refusal of thousand-li horses, repeatedly argued that the ruler should have no special likes, lest openings be given for those who watch and wait.
translations.idiomatic: In lecturing on how Emperor Wen of Han refused a thousand-li horse, Tangjie argued again and again that a ruler must not indulge private tastes, lest others seize the chance to pry and flatter.

sentences.zh: 自是每進講必原本經義，極論史事，歸於責難陳善。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he lectured he grounded himself in classical meaning, spoke fully on historical events, and returned to admonishing and offering good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every lecture returned to the classics, drew fully on history, and ended in frank admonition.

sentences.zh: 四年，恭親王被劾退出軍機，棠階謂王有定難功，時方多故，不當輕棄親賢，入對，力言王非有心之失。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Prince Gong was impeached and withdrew from the Grand Council; Tangjie said the prince had the merit of settling the crisis and that with troubles still many, one should not lightly cast aside a kinsman and worthy; at audience he strongly argued the prince's fault was not intentional.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 Prince Gong was impeached and left the Grand Council. Tangjie said the prince had saved the dynasty in crisis and must not be cast aside while troubles remained; at audience he insisted the fault was not deliberate.

sentences.zh: 會惇、醇兩王亦奏言奕訢不可遽罷，乃復命入直。

translations.literal: When the Princes of Dun and Chun also memorialized that Yixin must not be abruptly dismissed, he was again ordered to resume duty in the council.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princes of Dun and Chun also argued that Yixin must not be removed so hastily, he was ordered back to the council.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁戰歿曹州，棠階以朝廷賞多罰少，疆臣每存藐玩，上疏極言其弊，於是有申飭直省督撫之諭。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen died in battle at Caozhou, Tangjie, because the court rewarded much and punished little and frontier officials often held it in contempt, memorialized at length on the evil of this, and thereupon came an edict rebuking governors-general and governors of the metropolitan region and provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengge Rinchen fell at Caozhou, Tangjie argued that too many rewards and too few punishments made frontier governors careless; his memorial led to an edict rebuking provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 棠階自入直樞廷，軍書旁午，一事稍有未安，輒憂形於色。

translations.literal: From the time Tangjie entered duty in the council, military dispatches came in a flood; if anything was slightly unsettled, worry showed in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tangjie joined the council, dispatches poured in; the slightest setback showed in his face.

sentences.zh: 積勞致疾，十一月，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Accumulated labor brought on illness; in the eleventh month he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Worn down by overwork, he fell ill and died in the eleventh month, at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，遣貝勒載治奠醊，賜金治喪，贈太子太保，諡文清。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply shaken; he sent the prince Zaiye to offer libations, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously gave him the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and honored him with the posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: The court was stricken; Prince Zaiye was sent to offer libations, gold was granted for the funeral, and Tangjie was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent with the posthumous name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 棠階初入翰林，即潛心理學，嘗手鈔湯斌遺書以自勗。

translations.literal: When Tangjie first entered the Hanlin he devoted himself to Neo-Confucian learning and once copied Tang Bin's posthumous writings by hand to encourage himself.
translations.idiomatic: From his first days in the Hanlin, Tangjie immersed himself in Neo-Confucian study and once copied Tang Bin's posthumous writings by hand to spur himself on.

sentences.zh: 會通程、硃、陸、王學說，無所偏主，要以克己復禮、身體實行為歸。

translations.literal: He comprehended the teachings of Cheng, Zhu, Lu, and Wang without partial adherence, taking self-restraint and return to ritual and bodily practice as his aim.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the teachings of the Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, Lu Xiangshan, and Wang Yangming without partisan bias, and aimed always at self-restraint, return to ritual, and practice in the flesh.

sentences.zh: 日記自省，畢生不懈。

translations.literal: He kept a diary for self-examination and never slackened through life.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a diary of self-examination and never let the habit lapse.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，既貴，儉約無改。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor; once honored he did not change his frugality.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor, and even after he rose high he lived as frugally as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「憂患者生之門。

translations.literal: He once said: 'Suffering is the gate to life.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Hardship is the gate to life.

sentences.zh: 吾終身不敢忘忍飢待米時也！」

translations.literal: Through my life I dare not forget the time of enduring hunger and waiting for rice!'
translations.idiomatic: I dare never forget the days when I went hungry waiting for rice to arrive!"

sentences.zh: 吳廷棟，字竹如，安徽霍山人。

translations.literal: Wu Tingdong, style name Zhuru, was a native of Huoshan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong, styled Zhuru, came from Huoshan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光五年拔貢，授刑部七品小京官，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he was selected as a tribute student, appointed a seventh-rank junior secretary in the Board of Punishments, and promoted in succession to director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1825 he passed the tribute-student selection, entered the Board of Punishments as a junior secretary, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 廷棟少好宋儒之學，入官益植節厲行，蹇蹇自靖。

translations.literal: Tingdong from youth loved Song Neo-Confucian learning; on entering office he further cultivated integrity and stern conduct, upright and self-restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wu Tingdong loved Song Neo-Confucian learning; in office he grew only more upright and strict, holding himself apart with stubborn integrity.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，京察一等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he received the top grade in the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he received the top grade in the capital officials' evaluation.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎書元兼崇文門副監督，獲販私釀者三十六人，承審者以漏稅擬滿杖。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister Shuyuan concurrently supervised the Chongwen Gate; thirty-six persons caught selling illicit brew were tried, and the examining officials proposed the full penalty for tax evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Shuyuan was then deputy supervisor at Chongwen Gate when thirty-six illicit brewers were seized; the examiners proposed the maximum penalty for tax evasion.

sentences.zh: 已而覆訊得書元家人詐贓狀，部臣據以入奏。

translations.literal: On re-examination evidence emerged of extortion by Shuyuan's household; the ministry officials memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On re-examination, evidence of extortion by Shuyuan's household came out, and the ministries reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文宗疑書元孤立，降旨切責，會廷棟召對，上詢是獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong suspected Shuyuan was isolated and issued a stern edict of rebuke; when Tingdong was summoned for audience the Emperor inquired about the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng Emperor suspected Shuyuan was being singled out and rebuked the ministries sharply; when Wu Tingdong was called to audience, the emperor asked about the case.

sentences.zh: 廷棟從容敷奏，且詳陳治道之要，言利之害，君子小人之辨，上首肯，獄竟得解。

translations.literal: Tingdong calmly set forth his account and in detail explained the essentials of governing the Way, the harm of profit-seeking, and the distinction between gentlemen and petty men; the Emperor nodded assent and the case was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong answered calmly, then spoke at length on governing, the harm of chasing profit, and the difference between gentlemen and petty men. The emperor nodded, and the case was closed.

sentences.zh: 因詢廷棟讀何書，廷棟以程、硃對。

translations.literal: He then asked what books Tingdong read; Tingdong answered, Cheng and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he read; Wu Tingdong answered, the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「學程、硃者每多迂拘。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Those who study Cheng and Zhu are often rigid and constrained.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Students of Cheng and Zhu are often stiff and narrow."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此不善學之過。

translations.literal: He replied: 'That is the fault of not studying well.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That is the fault of studying badly.

sentences.zh: 程、硃以明德為體，新民為用，天下未有有體而無用者。

translations.literal: Cheng and Zhu take illustrious virtue as substance and renewing the people as function; under Heaven there has never been substance without function.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Zhu take illustrious virtue as root and renewing the people as use; nowhere is there root without use.

sentences.zh: 皇上讀書窮理，以裕知人之識；

translations.literal: Your Majesty reads books and exhausts principle to broaden the knowledge of discerning men;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reads to grasp principle, you will widen your eye for men;

sentences.zh: 清心寡欲，以養坐照之明。

translations.literal: purify the heart and lessen desires to nurture the clarity of seated illumination.
translations.idiomatic: purify your heart and curb desire, and you will nurture the clear sight that comes from stillness.

sentences.zh: 寤寐求賢，內外得人，天下何憂不治？」

translations.literal: Seek worthy men waking and sleeping; if within and without you gain the right men, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed?'
translations.idiomatic: Seek worthy men waking and sleeping; with the right men at court and in the provinces, how could the realm fail to be governed?'

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 尋出為直隸河間知府。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as prefect of Hejian in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Hejian in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 粵匪北犯畿輔，廷棟練民兵巡防，民倚以為固。

translations.literal: When Taiping rebels invaded north into the capital region, Tingdong trained militia for patrol and defense, and the people relied on him as a bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping forces pushed into the capital region, he trained militia for patrol and defense, and the people looked to him as their shield.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士勝保督師至河間，責供張甚急，知縣王灴迫於應付，自刎不殊。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat Academician Sengbao arrived at Hejian commanding troops and demanded supplies with great urgency; Magistrate Wang Hong, pressed to meet them, attempted suicide and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat Academician Sengbao arrived in command and demanded lavish supplies; Magistrate Wang Hong, crushed by the demand, tried to kill himself and barely survived.

sentences.zh: 廷棟詣大營陳其事，勝保矍然，飭部下聽命。

translations.literal: Tingdong went to the main camp and stated the matter; Sengbao started awake and ordered his subordinates to obey.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong went to the main camp and laid out the case; Sengbao was startled into restraint and ordered his men to obey.

sentences.zh: 連擢永定河道、直隸按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to commissioner of the Yongding River circuit and provincial surveillance commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in quick succession to Yongding River commissioner and Zhili provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以河間京師門戶，廷棟善守禦，得民心，仍留知府任。

translations.literal: Because Hejian was the gateway to the capital, Tingdong was skilled at defense and had won the people's hearts, he was kept in the prefect's post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hejian guarded the road to the capital and Wu Tingdong had won the people's trust through sound defense, he was kept on as prefect.

sentences.zh: 四年，軍事定，乃之按察使任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when military affairs were settled, he then took up the surveillance commissioner's post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854, once the fighting had settled, he took up his post as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to be provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was made Shandong provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時部臣奏請畿內賦稅兼收大錢鈔票各三成，上下交病，總督譚廷襄不敢言。

translations.literal: At the time ministry officials memorialized that taxes in the metropolitan region should collect thirty percent each in large cash and bank notes; all were afflicted above and below, and Governor Tan Tingxiang dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries then proposed that metropolitan taxes be collected thirty percent in large cash and thirty percent in bank notes; the scheme distressed everyone, and Governor Tan Tingxiang dared not object.

sentences.zh: 會廷棟入覲，面奏：「大錢鈔票實不流通。

translations.literal: When Tingdong came to audience he stated face to face: 'Large cash and bank notes in fact do not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Tingdong came to audience he said plainly, "Large cash and bank notes do not really circulate.

sentences.zh: 立法必先便於民方可行，必先信於民方能久。

translations.literal: In making laws one must first make them convenient for the people before they can be carried out; one must first win the people's trust before they can last.
translations.idiomatic: A law must first serve the people before it can work; it must first win their trust before it can endure.

sentences.zh: 今條科太多，朝夕更改，國家先不能自信，何以取信於民？」

translations.literal: Today there are too many statutes, changed morning and evening; the state itself cannot first have confidence—how can it win confidence from the people?'
translations.idiomatic: Too many rules change from day to day; the state cannot trust its own policy—how can the people?'

sentences.zh: 上首肯者再。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded assent twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded twice in agreement.

sentences.zh: 既而廷襄入朝，遂奏罷前議。

translations.literal: Before long Tingxiang came to court and memorialized to abolish the earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tan Tingxiang came to court and memorialized to drop the proposal.

sentences.zh: 山東吏治久窳，廷棟獎廉懲貪。

translations.literal: Shandong administration had long been corrupt; Tingdong rewarded integrity and punished greed.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong administration had long been rotten; Wu Tingdong rewarded the honest and punished the greedy.

sentences.zh: 方議海口立局收貨捐，持不可。

translations.literal: When a levy on goods at a bureau to be set up at the seaport was under discussion, he held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated a commodity levy at a new seaport bureau, he opposed it.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐奏銷遲誤，降補直隸按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for delay in reporting accounts, he was demoted and reassigned as Zhili surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he was demoted for late account submissions and reassigned as Zhili surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復調山東。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was transferred back to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，入為大理寺卿，尋擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he entered the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review and was soon promoted to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was recalled as president of the Court of Judicial Review and soon promoted to vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南平，廷棟上疏，略曰：「萬方之治亂在朝政，百工之敬肆視君心。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangnan was pacified, Tingdong memorialized, stating in part: 'Order and disorder throughout the realm lie in court governance; the diligence or laxity of all officials depends on the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when Jiangnan was pacified, Wu Tingdong memorialized: "Whether the realm is ordered or in chaos depends on the court; whether officials are diligent or lax depends on the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 事不貴文，貴其實；

translations.literal: In affairs what is valued is not ornament but substance;
translations.idiomatic: In affairs what matters is not fine words but substance;

sentences.zh: 下不從令，從所好。

translations.literal: subordinates do not follow orders but follow what is favored.
translations.idiomatic: subordinates do not follow orders—they follow what the ruler favors.

sentences.zh: 夫治亂決於敬肆，敬肆根於喜懼。

translations.literal: Order and disorder are decided by reverence or laxity; reverence and laxity root in joy and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder turn on reverence or laxity, and reverence or laxity grow from joy and fear.

sentences.zh: 自古功成志遂，人主喜心一生而驕心已伏，宦寺有乘其喜而貢諂媚者矣，左右有乘其喜而肆蒙蔽者矣，容悅之臣有因此而工諛佞者矣，屏逐之姦有因此而巧夤緣者矣。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when merit is achieved and aims fulfilled, once the ruler's heart of joy arises, the heart of pride is already lurking; eunuchs have those who seize on his joy to offer flattery, attendants at his side those who seize on his joy to indulge in deception, pleasing ministers who thereby become skilled in sycophancy, and banished villains who thereby craftily seek connections.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when success is won the ruler's joy awakens pride already waiting beneath it: eunuchs bring flattery, attendants deceive, pleasing ministers perfect their sycophancy, and exiled schemers claw their way back.

sentences.zh: 諂媚貢則柄暗竊，蒙蔽肆則權下移，諛佞工則主志惑，夤緣巧則宵小升。

translations.literal: When flattery is offered power is secretly stolen; when deception runs free authority shifts downward; when sycophancy is skilled the ruler's purpose is confused; when crafty connections succeed petty men rise.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery steals power in the dark; deception shifts authority downward; sycophancy clouds the ruler's mind; crafty connections raise petty men.

sentences.zh: 於是受蠱惑，塞聰明，遠老成，惡忠鯁。

translations.literal: Then one is bewitched, intelligence is blocked, the seasoned are kept far, and the loyal and blunt are hated.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler is bewitched, his judgment blocked, the seasoned pushed away, and the bluntly loyal despised.

sentences.zh: 從前戒懼之念，一喜敗之；

translations.literal: The former mind of caution and fear is ruined by a single joy;
translations.idiomatic: A single burst of joy undoes the habit of caution;

sentences.zh: 此後侈縱之行，一喜開之。

translations.literal: the later path of extravagance and license is opened by a single joy.
translations.idiomatic: and a single burst of joy opens the way to extravagance and license.

sentences.zh: 方且矜予智，樂莫違，逞獨斷，快從欲，一人肆於上，群小扇於下，流毒蒼生，貽禍社稷，稽諸史冊，後先一轍。

translations.literal: Just then one prides oneself on wisdom, delights in none opposing, indulges arbitrary decision, takes pleasure in following desires; one man is lax above and petty men fan it below, poison flows to the common people and calamity is bequeathed to the altars of soil and grain—search the historical records and the tracks before and after are one.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler prides himself on wisdom, delights in having his way, indulges arbitrary rule and his own desires; laxity above is fanned by petty men below, the people suffer, and the state is endangered—the histories show the same pattern again and again.

sentences.zh: 推原其端，祗一念由喜入驕而已。

translations.literal: Tracing it to the origin, it is only a single thought passing from joy into pride.
translations.idiomatic: Trace it to the root, and it is only one thought slipping from joy into pride.

sentences.zh: 軍興以來，十數省億萬生靈慘遭鋒鏑，即倡亂之奸民，何一非朝廷赤子？

translations.literal: Since the raising of armies, in a dozen provinces hundreds of millions have bitterly suffered blade and arrow—even the wicked commoners who began rebellion, which of them were not the court's own children?
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, tens of millions in a dozen provinces have suffered under arms—even those who rose in rebellion were once the court's own children.

sentences.zh: 大兵所加，盡被誅夷。

translations.literal: Where great armies struck, all were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Where imperial armies struck, multitudes were cut down.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇上體上天好生之心，必有哀矜不忍喜者。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and the Emperor, embodying Heaven's heart of cherishing life, must surely have compassion and cannot bear to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and emperor, sharing Heaven's love of life, must feel compassion and cannot rejoice.

sentences.zh: 況旗兵乏食，根本空虛，新疆缺餉，邊陲搖動。

translations.literal: Moreover banner troops lack food, the foundation is hollow, Xinjiang lacks pay, and the frontier is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Banner troops lack food, the dynasty's foundations are hollow, Xinjiang lacks pay, and the frontiers are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 兼之強鄰偪處，邪教肆行，豈惟不可喜，而實屬可懼。

translations.literal: Added to this, powerful neighbors press close and heterodox sects run rampant—not only may one not rejoice, but there is real cause for fear.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful neighbors press close and heterodox sects run wild—not only is there no cause for joy, but real cause for fear.

sentences.zh: 假使萬幾之馀，或有一念之肆，臣工效之，視彰癉為故事，輕告戒為具文，積習相沿，工為粉飾，將仍成為叢脞怠荒之局矣。

translations.literal: Suppose amid the myriad affairs there were a single thought of laxity—officials would imitate it, treat reward and punishment as routine, treat admonitions as empty documents, entrenched habits would continue, ornament would be crafted, and again there would be a tangle of petty matters, laxity, and neglect.
translations.idiomatic: If amid ten thousand affairs a single lax thought arose, officials would follow: rewards and punishments would become routine, warnings mere paper, old habits would continue, and ornament would replace substance—until the court sank again into petty bustle and neglect.

sentences.zh: 是非堅定刻苦，持之以恆，積數十年恭儉憂勤，有未易培國脈復元氣者。

translations.literal: Unless one is firm and arduous and holds to it without cease, accumulating decades of reverence, frugality, worry, and diligence, the nation's vital pulse is not easily cultivated nor its vital energy restored.
translations.idiomatic: Only firm resolve, hardship borne without cease, and decades of reverence, frugality, worry, and diligence can slowly rebuild the nation's strength.

sentences.zh: 夫上行必下效，內治則外安，而其道莫大於敬，其幾必始於懼。

translations.literal: What is above must be imitated below; when inner governance is sound the outer is secure—and in this Way nothing is greater than reverence, and its beginning must lie in fear.
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler does, officials follow; sound rule within brings peace without—and nothing is greater than reverence, which must begin in fear.

sentences.zh: 懼天命無常，則不敢恃天；

translations.literal: Fear that Heaven's mandate is inconstant, and one dare not rely on Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Fear Heaven's mandate is inconstant, and you will not presume on Heaven;

sentences.zh: 懼民碞可畏，則不敢玩民。

translations.literal: fear that the people's anger is formidable, and one dare not trifle with the people.
translations.idiomatic: fear the people's wrath, and you will not trifle with the people.

sentences.zh: 懼者敬之始，敬者懼之終。

translations.literal: Fear is the beginning of reverence; reverence is the end of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fear is where reverence begins; reverence is where fear ends.

sentences.zh: 大智愈明，神武愈彰，紹祖宗富有之大業，開子孫無疆之丕基，是皆由皇心之懼始而敬成也。

translations.literal: Great wisdom grows clearer, divine martial prowess shines forth, the abundant enterprise of the ancestors is continued, and an unbounded foundation is opened for posterity—all this begins in the imperial heart's fear and is completed in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Great wisdom grows clearer, martial glory brighter, the ancestors' vast enterprise is carried on, and an endless foundation laid for posterity—all beginning in the ruler's fear and fulfilled in reverence.

sentences.zh: 易曰：'危者使平，易者使傾，懼以終始，其要無咎。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'What is perilous is made level; what is easy is made to topple; with fear from beginning to end, the essential is freedom from blame.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, 'What is perilous is made level; what is easy is made to topple; hold fear from start to finish, and blame will be avoided.'

sentences.zh: '詩曰：'敬之敬之，天維顯思！

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Revere it, revere it—Heaven clearly considers this!'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'Revere it, revere it—Heaven clearly sees!'

sentences.zh: '可弗以為永鑑歟？」

translations.literal: May this not serve as an eternal mirror?"
translations.idiomatic: Should this not be an everlasting mirror?"

sentences.zh: 疏上，優詔嘉納，命存其疏於弘​​德殿以備省覽。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict praised and accepted it, and he was ordered to keep the memorial in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict warmly praised it and ordered it kept in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for the emperor's reading.

sentences.zh: 皇太后召對時，諭曰：「皇帝衝齡踐阼，國家大事，汝宜直言無隱，以無負先帝知遇。」

translations.literal: When the empress dowager summoned him for audience she instructed: 'The Emperor is young in acceding to the throne; on great affairs of state you should speak frankly without concealment, so as not to fail the late Emperor's gracious trust.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience the empress dowager told him, "The emperor is young on the throne; on great affairs of state speak frankly and hold nothing back, so as not to betray the late emperor's trust in you."

sentences.zh: 廷棟感激出涕。

translations.literal: Tingdong, moved to gratitude, wept.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，許之，歸寓江寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on grounds of age and illness he begged retirement; it was granted, and he took up residence in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he asked to retire on account of age and illness; permission was granted, and he settled in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he died, at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，詔褒其廉靜自持，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: When his death memorial entered, an edict praised his integrity and quiet self-restraint and granted condolence payments according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial reached the throne; an edict praised his integrity and self-restraint and granted the usual mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 直隸、山東皆祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: In Zhili and Shandong he was both enshrined in shrines to famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to him as a renowned official were erected in both Zhili and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 廷棟學以不欺為本。

translations.literal: Tingdong's learning took not deceiving as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong's learning rested on refusing self-deception.

sentences.zh: 官臬司時，畿輔連有逆倫獄，總督慮一月頻入奏幹上怒，廷棟曰：「此吾儕不能教化之過，待罪不暇，敢欺飾耶？」

translations.literal: When he was provincial judge, the capital region had successive cases of violation of human relations; the governor feared that frequent memorials in one month would provoke the Emperor's anger. Tingdong said: 'This is our failure to teach and transform; we have no leisure to await punishment—how dare we deceive and cover up?'
translations.idiomatic: As provincial judge he faced a string of parricide cases in the capital region; the governor feared too many memorials in one month would anger the throne. Wu Tingdong said, "This is our failure to teach the people—we are already at fault; how dare we cover it up?"

sentences.zh: 及去官，僑居清貧，不受餽遺。

translations.literal: When he left office he lived abroad in clean poverty and accepted no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived modestly in retirement and accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 著有拙修集十卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Clumsy Cultivation Collection in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Clumsy Cultivation Collection in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 論曰：倭仁晚為兩宮所敬禮，際會中興，輔導衝主，兢兢於君心敬肆之間，當時舉朝嚴憚，風氣賴以維持。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Wo Ren in his later years was honored by the two palaces; meeting the Restoration, he assisted and guided the young sovereign, scrupulous between reverence and laxity in the ruler's heart; at the time the whole court stood in awe, and public morals were maintained thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In his later years Wo Ren was revered by the two empress dowagers. At the restoration he tutored a boy emperor, ever watchful over the balance of reverence and laxity in the ruler's heart; the whole court stood in awe of him, and public morals were steadied by his example.

sentences.zh: 惟未達世變，於自強要政，鄙夷不屑言，後轉為異論者所藉口。

translations.literal: Only he did not comprehend the changes of the age; toward essential policies of self-strengthening he showed contempt and disdained to speak of them, and later this became a pretext for those of other views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not grasp how the world was changing; on the policies needed for self-strengthening he showed contempt and would not speak of them, and later advocates of new doctrines used that as their excuse.

sentences.zh: 李棠階、吳廷棟正色立朝，不負所學，翕然笙磬同音，而棠階尤平實持大體，可謂體用兼備矣。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong stood with stern countenance at court, not failing their learning, harmonious as pipes and stones in one tone; Tangjie especially was plain and practical and held to the larger pattern—one may say substance and function were both complete.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong stood upright at court, true to their learning, in harmony like tuned pipes and chimes; Tangjie especially was plain, practical, and steady on the larger pattern—men in whom substance and practice were one.
